FOREVVORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 1) vvas adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Furniture Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


The Government of India, State Governments and University Grants Commission have under way extensive 
schemes for the development of library facilities and the setting up of new libraries in various parts of the 
country, keeping this in view IS 1553 : 1989 ‘Design of library buildings — Recommendations relating to its 
primary elements’ was prepared to serve as a guide relating to basic elements of design pertaining to library 
buildings. As the next step it was felt that the furniture and fittings that go into making the library functional 
and useful should also be appropriately designed and the minimum requirements laid down. This standard 
lays down the general requirements of items of timber furniture used in libraries, leaving enough scope for the 
designer to vary the actual shape, aesthetics, etc. 


This standard was first published in 1961 and then revised in 1978. In this revision the following changes 
have been effected: 


a) Latest specifications for various types of timber used in the manufacture of library furniture and 
fittings have been included. 


b) All the amendments to previous version have been absorbed. 
c) Loading requirements of shelves of book rack have been modified. 
d) Referred Indian Standards have been updated. 


This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards covering requirements of libraries. 


A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as ECO-Mark is also included. The ECO-Mark 
would be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the B/S Act, 1986 as per the Resolution 
No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 and No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government 
of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with ECO logo, it shall also carry the ISI Mark of BIS besides 
meeting additional optional environment friendly requirements. For this purpose, the Standard Mark of BIS 
would be a single mark being a combination of the ISI Mark and the ECO logo. Requirements to be satisfied 
for a product to qualify for the BIS Standard Mark for ECO friendliness will be optional; manufacturing units 
will be free to opt for the ISI Mark alone also. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding of numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1829 (Part 1) : 2017 


Indian Standard 
LIBRARY FURNITURE AND FITTINGS — SPECIFICATION 


PART 1 TIMBER 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements for the 
following items of wooden furniture meant for use in 
a library: 


a) Unit book rack, 

b) Bay guide holder, 

c) Book trolley, 

d) Catalogue cards tray and cabinet, 
e) Catalogue cards box, 

f) Catalogue cards work tray, 
g) Control region fittings, 

h) Charging trays, 

j) Reading room table, 

k) Study table, 

m) Periodicals display rack, 
n) Chairs, and 

p) Display stand. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged 
to investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards indicated at Annex A. 


3 MATERIALS 


3.1 Wood particle boards required for the 
manufacture of various items of furniture shall 
conform to IS 3087 and shall be of type FPS or 
FPT-1, that is, flat pressed single-layer board or flat 
pressed three-layer board. Wood particle board used 
for wooden racks, cabinets, etc, which require baking 
paints or enamel finishes shall be manufactured with 
only BWR type of adhesives like phenol 
formaldehyde. 


3.1.1 For ECO-Mark, the particle board shall conform 
to the requirements specified in IS 3087 for 
ECO-Mark purposes. 


3.2 Veneered particle boards shall conform to IS 3097. 
Both grades of veneered particle boards can be used 
where the furniture items are to be finished with air- 
drying paints, or varnishes. Where oven-baking 
paints, enamel or varnishes are to be used, only 
exterior grade veneered particle boards shall be used. 


3.2.1 For ECO-Mark, the veneered particle board 
shall conform to the requirements specified in IS 3097 
for ECO-Mark purposes. 


3.3 Plywood 


3.3.1 Plywood used in the manufacture of various 
items of furniture and fittings for use in libraries shall 
conform to IS 303. Any of the two grades, namely 
BWR and MR of plywood may be used for items 
which are to be finished with air-drying paints, 
enamel or varnishes. Where items are finished with 
oven-drying paints, enamel or varnishes, only BWR 
grade of plywood shall be used. The plywood used 
shall not be interior to Type BB. In case veneered 
plywood is used it shall conform to 181328. 


3.3.2 For ECO-Mark, the plywood shall conform to 
the requirements specified in IS 303 for ECO-Mark 
purposes. 


3.4 Blockboards 


Blockboards shall conform to IS 1659 and shall be of 
MR Grade. 


3.4.1 For ECO-Mark, the block board shall conform 
to the requirements specified in IS 1659 for 
ECO-Mark purposes. 


3.5 Timber 


Any species of timber specified in IS 13622 shall be 
used in the manufacture of library furniture and 
fittings. 


3.5.1 For ECO-Mark, only species of timber as 
specified in IS 13622 from sources other than natural 
forests, such as, timber from individual and social 
forestry plantations, shade trees from tea and coffee 
estates, etc, shall be used for the manufacture of 
library furniture and fittings. 


IS 1829 (Part 1) : 2017 


3.6 Medium Density Fibre Boards (MDF) 


MDF where used for the manufacture of various 
items of furniture fittings for use in library having 
flat surfaces shall conform to IS 12406. 


3.6.1 For ECO-Mark, the medium density fibre 
board shall conform to the requirements specified 
in IS 12406 for ECO-Mark purposes. 


3.7 Adhesive 


Adhesive used for joinery work shall conform to 
IS 851, IS 852 or IS 4835. 


3.8 Wood Screws 
Wood screws shall conform to IS 6760. 


3.9 Paints, enamels and varnishes shall conform 
to the relevant Indian Standards, wherever they 
exist, for air-drying as well as stoving finishes. 
Finishing shall conform to IS 4597, IS 2338 (Part 1) 
and IS 2338 (Part 2). 


4 UNIT BOOK RACKS 
4.1 Terminology 


For the purpose of this standard the following 
definitions shall apply. 


4.1.1 Bay — The part of the face of a rack between 
two consecutive uprights. 


4.1.2 Double Faced Unit Rack — A rack consisting 
of three uprights forming four open bays, two on 
each face. 


4.1.3 Label Holder — A groove along the front 
edge of the shelf plank designed to hold the shelf 
label so as to allow its movement from end to end. 


4.1.4 Partition or Bay Stop — A divider fitted 
between the bay-pairs opening into the two 
opposite sides of a unit book rack. 


4.1.5 Shelf Plank — A horizontal support for 
books, spanning a bay. 


4.1.6 Single Faced Unit Rack — A rack consisting 
of three uprights forming two bays. 


4.1.7 Upright — A vertical supporting element of 
arack. 


4.2 Dimensions and Tolerances 


4.2.1 The overall dimensions of the unit book racks 
shall be as given in Table 1. Generally 350 mm 
centre-to-centre distance should be adopted for 
shelves. 


4.2.2 Tolerances 


The overall dimensions specified in Table 1 shall not 
vary by more than +5 mm. 


4.2.3 The vvooden book racks shall be rectangular 
at all the measurable surfaces vvithin a tolerance of 
+8 mm between the two diagonals of the rectangle.

4.3 Fabrication 


4.3.1 Each bay shall have seven shelf planks out of 
which three (the topmost, central and the bottommost) 
shall be fixed and four shall be adjustable. 


NOTE — The heavy and outsize books should be kept on 
their aides instead of on their bottom edges. 


4.3.2 Uprights 
The uprights shall be of not less than 35 mm thickness. 
4.3.3 Single Faced Unit Racks 


Single faced unit racks shall be fabricated according 
to the specifications prescribed in 5 of IS 7070. 


4.3.4 Double Faced Unit Racks 


4.3.4.1 A typical illustration of a double faced unit 
rack is shown in Fig. 1. 


4.3.4.2 Shelf planks 


The thickness of shelf planks shall be not less than 
25 mm. The depth of the shelf plank on top, centre and 
bottom of the rack shall be 450 mm. The depth of the 
adjustable shelf plank shall be 220 mm to allow space 
for the partition to be inserted between the bay pairs, 
opening into opposite faces. 


4.3.4.3 Partition 


To prevent the books in one face from getting mixed 
up with those of the other face, a partition (or bay 
stop) shall be provided. The partition shall start from 
the bottom of the topmost fixed plank and stop 15 cm 
above the top of the bottommost fixed plank. 


4.3.5 Label Holder 


Label holder shall be wrought along the front edge of 
each shelf plank and shall admit card strips 15 mm

4.4 Loading 
Shelves shall be designed to carry a load of, 
a) For single faced (depth 300 mm): 


1) 0.054 kg/mm length (54 kg per bay that 
is 1 000 mm length) for 7 days with 
maximum 4 mm deflection at center 
under loaded condition. 

2) 0.09 kg/mm length (90 kg per bay that is 
1 000 mm length) for 15 min without any 
sudden breakage or loss of structural 
integrity. 


b) For double faced (depth 450 mm): 


1) 0.09 kg/mm length (90 kg per bay that is 
1000 mm length) for 7 days with 
maximum 4 mm deflection under loaded 
condition. 


2) 0.13 kg/mm length (130 kg per bay that 
is 1 000 mm length) for 15 min without 
any accidental breakage or loss of 
structural integrity. 


5 BAY GUIDE HOLDERS 


5.1 The external dimensions of bay guide holders 
shall be 400 mm x 200 mm. It shall be provided with a 
groove arrangement so that the guide could be slid 


along the length. It shall also have hooks for 
suspension from a rod or from rings above. 


6 BOOK TROLLEY 


6.1 The essential features of a book trolley are 
shown in Fig. 2. 


6.2 The trolley shall have two pairs of sloping 
shelves and one flat bottom shelf for books of large 
size. 


6.3 The height of the trolley shall be 750 mm the 
same as that of a table. 


6.4 The planks shall be suitably supported such as 
by iron rods and the uprights rigidly connected to 
each other and shall fulfil the loading requirements 
specified under 4.4. 


6.5 Suitable protection may be provided at the 
bottom corners and the ends ofuprights to minimize 
damage due to knocking against other furniture or 
fittings or walls or pillars. 


6.6 The trolley shall be fitted with four rubber tyred 
ball-bearing wheels; one of the swivelling type at 
each end and two of the fixed type in the centre. 


7 CATALOGUE CARDS TRAY AND CABINET 


7.1 Dimensions and Construction of Catalogue 
Cards Tray 


7.1.1 The size of catalogue cards tray is based on 
the card size of 125 mm x 75 mm (International 
catalogue card size). 


IS 1829 (Part 1) : 2017 


7.1.2 Each tray shall be constructed as shown in 
Fig. 3. 


7.1.2.1 The external dimensions of the tray shall be 
155 mm x 100 mm x 430 mm. The side and back planks 
shall be 12 mm thick and 55 mm high. The front plank 
ofthe tray shall be 155 mm vvide and 100 mm high. 


7.1.2.2 A central strip (not shown in Fig. 3) shall be 
provided at the bottom of the tray to receive a device 
to prevent the sliding of the card rest. It shall be 
30 mm x 5 mm. 


7.1.2.3 The bottom of the tray shall also be fitted 
with two reapers 25 mm x 5 mm (not shown), properly 
centred and inter-connected. The bottom shall not 
be covered in order to prevent collection of dust. 


7.1.2.4 A brass rod or a rod of similar corrosion 
resisting material, 5 mm in diameter shall be fitted 
right through the centre of tray to lock up the cards. 
A knob shall be screwed to the rod projecting through 
the face plank, to permit pulling out of the rod. The 
rod shall be held at the back of the plank with a hook. 


7.1.2.5 To prevent the tray from being accidently 
pulled entirely out of the socket, a self-locking 
gravity catch shall be fixed suitably. 


7.1.2.6 A brass label holder shall be provided at the 
face plank just above the centre. The face plank may 
also be fitted with a knob or a handle to pull the tray. 


7.1.2.7 A movable card rest with a hole in the 
appropriate position for the brass rod to pass through

7.2 Dimensions and Construction of Catalogue 
Cards Cabinet 


7.2.1 The cabinet shall consist of two parts: 


a) The cabinet, and 
b) The stand on which the cabinet rests. 


7.2.2 Dimensions 


The dimensions of the cabinet shall depend upon 
the number of trays it carries. The overall dimensions 
of the catalogue cards cabinets having different 
number of trays shall be as given in Table 2. 


7.2.3 Construction 


a) A typical illustration of the cabinet 
consisting of 36 trays in 6 columns of 6 trays 
each is shown in Fig. 4. 

b) The planks used for the sides, back, bottom 
and top shall be 20 mm thick. 


c) The front of the cabinet shall be divided into 
six vertical columns by means of five 
intermediate planks 20 mm thick and 100 mm 
wide. 

d) The front of the columns shall be connected 
with the back of the cabinet by pairs of cross 
bearers at regular intervals to give a clear 
socket opening for the tray to fit in. The 
cross bearer shall have 20 mm thickness and 
25 mm width. 

e) Suitable arrangements shall be made to lock 
at least two consecutive columns by one 
device. 


f) A pull out slide, where desired, may be 
provided within the cabinet. 
8 CATALOGUE CARDS BOX 


8.1 The catalogue cards box shall be constructed 
as shown in Fig. 5. 


IS 1829 (Part 1) : 2017 


8.2 The box and its lid shall be of equal height, so 
that when fully open each of them rests on the table 
top. 


8.3 The bottom part shall be provided with a brass 
label holder and a pair of flat brass hooks. The lid 
shall have the eyes to take the hooks. 


9 CATALOGUE CARDS WORK TRAY 


9.1 Catalogue cards work tray is functionally the 
same as the catalogue cards box but it is more like a 
tray (see Fig. 6). A fixed and a movable card rest shall 
be provided as in 7.1.2.7. 


10 CONTROL REGION FITTINGS 
10.1 Control Region 


10.1.1 The size of control region shall depend on 
the following: 


a) Size of library, 
b) Clientele of the library, 
c) Number of books issued out, and 


d) Records to be maintained at the counter. 


10.1.2 The dimensions of control region shall 
depend on number of persons operating the control 
region. The essential dimensions required to enable 
operation per person shall be as indicated in Fig. 7. 


10.2 Counter 


The counter shall have three shelves all round except 
at places intended to be occupied by the circulation 
staff as shown in Fig. 7, where kneehole space, 
600 mm wide, shall be provided. 


10.2.1 At a height of 135 cm from the ground there 
shall be a transparent plate shelf or a vvooden shelf 
vvith plastic laminates all around. This shelf shall be 
cantilevered and there shall be no vertical support 
near the vvorking edge of the counter so that an un- 
interrupted space is available on the counter deck 
for free movement of trays. The vertical barrier 
between the counter deck and the shelf at the farther

10.3 Control Gates 


The control gates shall consist of either a single leaf 
door with a gravity hinge or another similar device. 
The clear passage when the central gate is open, 
shall be approximately 500 mm. 


11 CHARGING TRAYS 


11.1 Charging trays are meant for containing readers’ 
tickets. The trays may have one, two, three or four 
compartments. 


11.2 The essential dimensions of the charging trays 
depend upon the size of the tickets issued. The 
overall dimensions of various trays shall be 
according to Newark Charging System or Browne 
Charging System as given in Table 3. The outer 
planks shall be of 18 mm thickness and the inner 
partitions for making compartments shall be 12 mm 
thick. 


12 READING ROOM TABLE 


12.1 The size of the reading room table shall be 
900 mm x 600 mm for single and 2 400 mm x 600 mm 
for three readers. A typical illustration of the reading 
room table is shown in Fig. 8. The height of the table 
top shall be 750 mm.

12.2 Kneehole Space 


The minimum kneehole space per reader shall be 
450 mm deep, 650 mm high and 600 mm wide. 


12.3 Foot Rest 


The footrest, either in the form of a fixed rod or as a 
separate pipe shall be provided at the height of 
150 mm from the floor. 


13 STUDY TABLE 


13.1 Study table shall have the same dimensions as 
the reading room table for a single reader, that is, 
900 mm x 600 mm. It may have additional provisions 
for the follovving: 
a) Side dravvers vvith locking arrangement, and 
b) Shelf space for keeping documents on the 
top of the table with lighting arrangement. 


13.2 Atypical illustration of the study table is shown 
in Fig. 9. 


14 PERIODICALS DISPLAY RACK 


14.1 A typical illustration of a periodicals display 
rack is shown in Fig. 10. 


14.2 Dimensions 


The overall dimensions of the periodicals display 
rack shall be as follows: 

a) Height — 1 850 - 1 900 mm, and 

b) Depth — 405 -- 10mm 


14.3 Construction 


A periodicals display rack shall consist of tvventy 
five compartments in five rows. Each compartment 
shall be of the size 265 + 10 mm x 345 + 10 mm and it 
shall be fitted with display shelf having a handle 
cum label holder. 


14.3.1 The outer sides of the rack shall be of 18 mm 
thick wooden board. The uprights, top and bottom 
shelves shall also be made of wooden board of 18 mm 
thickness. Intermediate horizontal shelves shall 
be of 12 mm commercial ply and the display shelves 
shall be of wooden wood frame with 5 mm wooden ply. 


15 CHAIRS 


15.1 The essential dimensions of wooden chairs 
shall be as given in 15.1.1 to 15.1.6 read with Fig. 11. 


15.1.1 The height of the seat of the chair above floor 
level shall be 430 mm. 


15.1.2 Effective Depth of Seat 


Maximum effective depth of the seat shall be 450 mm. 
This shall be measured from a vertical line through 
the centre of the front edge of the seat to a vertical 
line through the centre of the back edge of the seat. 


15.1.3 Seat Slope 


The seat shall be either horizontal or sloping 
downwards between 2° to 3°, from front to back. 


15.1.4 Width of Seat 


The minimum width of the seat shall be 450 mm.

15.1.5 Arm-Rests 


The minimum distance between the insides of the 
arms should be not less than 460 mm. The height of 
the elbow rest above the effective seat height shall 
be 200 mm. The arm rest may have a setback of 75 mm 
from the front edge of the seat. 


15.1.6 Height of Back Rest 


The height of back rest above the top of the seat 
shall be 450 mm. 


15.2 The chairs shall be fitted with noise-prevention 
pads in the legs. 


15.3 The chair seats shall not be hard or upholstered 
but shall preferably be of woven material to ensure 
ventilation and slight yielding when in use. 


15.4 The back rest of the chair shall be curved in 
plan or so shaped to give comfort to the body. It 


11 


shall neither be too curved to restrict the movement 
of the back nor be too flat. 


15.5 The height of the seat for counter chair shall 
depend upon the height of the counter. 


16 DISPLAY STAND 


16.1 Display stand shall be of 910 mm x 910 mm or 
1 220 mm x 1 220 mm size. It shall be made of any soft 
surface board like perforated board, straw board, etc. 
It shall be capable of holding pins. 


16.2 Display stand may either be single or double 
as required. 

17 FINISHING 

17.1 Wood Panel Components 


Wood panel components shall be given a coat of 
primer paint and filler. Wood putty shall be applied 


IS 1829 (Part 1) : 2017 


1320 


1850 TO 1900 


100 


All dimensions in millimetres. 


Fic. 10 TYPICAL ILLUSTRATION OF PERIODICAL DİSPLAY RACK 


to all the surfaces requiring filling and shall conform 
to the relevant Indian Standards. After preparing the 
surfaces two coats of enamel or paint, that is, one 
under-coat and one finishing coat shall be given. 
Alternatively, the surfaces may be stained and 
polished. The finishing coat shall be of synthetic 
air-drying enamel or stoving enamel for wood work. 
The enamel or paint shall be of exterior type and of a 
finish and colour as required (see also 3.9). 


17.1.1 In case of stoving enamels or paints, the 
components of the finished furniture items shall be 
stored at suitable temperature and for suitable time 
as advised by the manufacturer of the enamel. 


17.2 The finish shall be smooth, uniformly applied 
and free from visible defects. It shall be well based 
and shall not readily chip or flake. The dry film 
thickness shall be not less than 0.10 mm. 


17.3 All other components shall be finished in 
colour as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. 


12 


18 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR ECO- 
MARK 


18.1 General Requirements 


18.1.1 The product shall conform to the 
requirements of quality and performance as specified 
in the standard. 


18.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to BIS 
environmental consent clearance from the concerned 
State Pollution Control Board as per the provisions 
of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) 
Act, 1974 and Air (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1981 along with the authorization, if 
required under the Environment (Protection) Act, 
1986, while applying for ECO-Mark. 


18.2 Specific Requirements 


The product shall conform to the specific 
requirements given for ECO-Mark under the relevant 
clauses of this standard.

19 MARKING 


19.1 The library furniture and fittings shall be 
marked with a suitable mark identifying the 
manufacturer. 


13 


19.2 They may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 


19.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed 
by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made there 
under. The details of conditions under which a license 
for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in course of implementing the standard, 
of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be 
addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 35 (8070).
